title: Normalized pointed-etale stalk presentations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale site and module sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme map $p:T\to X$, a pointed etale neighbourhood is a scheme etale chart $U\to X$ with a map $T\to U$ over $X$; its arrows commute with the pointing. For a presheaf of commutative rings $R$ on this site, a normalized stalk presentation consists of a ring $R_p$ with a colimit cocone from the opposite neighbourhood diagram of $R$, a functor from presheaves of $R$-modules to $R_p$-modules, and for every module a colimit cocone of its underlying additive groups. Require the module functor maps and the scalar action to agree with the germ maps. A geometric stalk family provides such a presentation for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ and point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$; it includes the sheaf condition on $R$, exactness (preservation of finite limits and colimits) on module sheaves, and detection of isomorphisms by this family. These are presentation data and their defining equations, with no existence assertion. The regular-functions ring presheaf is $U\mapsto\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$.
